sentences.text:
Heard Sri Rakesh Kumar Porwal, learned counsel for the appellant and Sri Radhey Shyam,
learned counsel for the respondent no.2.

No one is present on behalf of the claimant-respondent no.1.
3.

First Appeal From Order No.433 of 2010 under Section 173 of Motor Vehicle Act, 1988 has been filed on behalf of owner of the vehicle against the judgement and award dated 09.12.2009 passed by Motor Accident Claims Tribunal/Special Judge (SC/ST Act), Etawah in MAC No.787 of 2007 by which compensation of Rs.2,58,100/- along with 6% interest has been awarded on account of death of Kuldeep, who died in road accident on 27.10.2007 and liability of payment has been fixed upon the appellant, who is owner of the vehicle.

entities.label: CASE_NUMBER

sentences.text:
4. First appeal from order No.432 of 2010 has been filed on behalf of owner of the vehicle against the judgement and award of Claims Tribunal dated 09.12.2009 passed in M.A.C.P. No.786 of 2007 by which compensation of Rs.6,42,924/- along with 6% interest on account of death of Ram Singh.
5.

Since, both the appeals are arising out of same accident and involves common issues, therefore,
both the appeals are decided together.

6. It is submitted by the learned counsel for the appellant that the car of the appellant bearing No.UP75 D 4857 was duly insured with respondent no.1- National Insurance Company Ltd. on the date of incident.
It is further submitted that the vehicle was insured by private car policy and package, which covers occupant of the vehicle.
Admittedly the deceased in both the appeals were travelling in car.

The learned Claims Tribunal has earned in fixing the liability upon the appellant holding that the passenger of the vehicle are not covered under the insurance policy ignoring the fact that it is a comprehensive package policy and occupant of the vehicle are also covered under the insurance policty.

He has placed reliance upon the judgement of Hon'ble Apex Court in the case of National Insurance Company Ltd. Vs. Balakrishan and another report in 2013 (1) TAC 1.
7.

entities.text: National Insurance Company Ltd. Vs. Balakrishan and another report in 2013 (1) TAC 1
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: On the other hand, learned counsel appearing for the National Insurance Company has not disputed that the vehicle of appellant was insured on the date of accident under the comprehensive package policy.

It is submitted that no extra premium was received by the insurance company to cover the risk of occupant of the vehicle and as such the claims Tribunal has rightly fixed the liability upon the appellant, who is owner of the vehicle.
8.

Considered the submission of learned counsel for the parties and perused the record.
9.
It is admitted that the deceased of both the claim petition were traveling in car bearing No.UP75 D 4857 and died on account of injuries received by them in a road accident on 27.10.2007.
The insurance policy of the aforesaid car has been annexed as Annexure No.1 to the affidavit filed in support of memo of appeal, which reflects that the vehicle was insured under the package policy.
This issue has been considered by the judgment of Hon'ble Apex Court in the case of National Insurance Company Ltd. (supra).
The relevant paragraph nos.21 & 22 of the judgement is reproduced here-in-blow:-

Subhash Chandra vs Smt. Sukhdevi And Another on 6 May, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/143610397/
2 "21.

entities.text: Subhash Chandra vs Smt. Sukhdevi And Another on 6 May, 2025 Indian Kanoon
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: In view of the aforesaid factual position, there is no scintilla of doubt that a "comprehensive/package policy" would cover the liability of the insurer for payment of compensation for the occupant in a car.

There is no cavil that an "Act Policy"
stands on a different footing from a "Comprehensive/Package Policy".

As the circulars have made the position very clear and the IRDA, which is presently the statutory authority, has commanded the insurance companies stating that a "Comprehensive/Package Policy" covers the liability, there cannot be any dispute in that regard.
We may hasten to clarify that the earlier pronouncements were rendered in respect of the "Act Policy" which admittedly cannot cover a third party risk of an occupant in a car.
But, if the policy is a "Comprehensive/Package Policy", the liability would be covered.

These aspects were not noticed in the case of Bhagyalakshmi and,
therefore, the matter was referred to a larger Bench.

We are disposed to think that there is no necessity to refer the present matter to a larger Bench as the IRDA, which is presently the statutory authority, has clarified the position by issuing circulars which have been reproduced in the judgment by the Delhi High Court and we have also reproduced the same.
22. In view of the aforesaid legal position, the question that emerges for consideration is whether in the case at hand, the policy is an "Act Policy" or "Comprehensive/Package Policy".
There has been no discussion either by the tribunal or the High Court in this regard.
True it is, before us, Annexure P-1 has been filed which is a policy issued by the insurer.

It only mentions the policy to be a "comprehensive policy" but we are inclined to think that there has to be a scanning of the terms of the entire policy to arrive at the conclusion whether it is really a "package policy" to cover the liability of an occupant in a car."
10.
The law has been settled by Hon'ble Apex Court that if the vehicle was insured under the comprehensive/package policy, the risk of occupant of the vehicle are also covered.

The Claims tribunal has committed illegality in fixing the liability upon the appellant, who is owner of the vehicle whereas the risk of occupant of the vehicle is fully covered under the insurance policy.
11. In view of the above discussion, both the First Appeal From Order filed on behalf of the appellant being owner of the vehicle are allowed.

The judgment and award of Claims Tribunal dated 09.12.2009 passed in both the claim petitions are modified to the extent that the insurance company- respondent no.1 is liable to pay compensation to the claimants.
12. Rs.25,000/- or any other amount deposited by the appellant in compliance of interim order dated 10.02.2010 be refunded to the appellant without furnishing any sureties in both the appeals.
